**Stochastika** is a blog about Probability and Statistics, written for students, engineers and anyone who wants to understand the ideas rather than memorise formulas.

## Why "Stochastika"?

The English word *stochastic* comes from the Greek verb **στοχάζομαι** (*stochazomai*), meaning "to aim at" or "to conjecture". Something stochastic cannot be predicted with certainty, but it can be reasoned about. That is exactly what Probability and Statistics do.

## How it is organised

The posts follow the structure of a university course in Probability and Statistics, from random experiments and sample spaces to hypothesis testing, and then on to time-series analysis. Each post combines:

- intuition and rigorous definitions,
- **R** examples with code you can run,
- **interactive** elements to experiment with the ideas,
- review questions.

## Who writes it

The content is based on the teaching material of **Epameinondas Diamantopoulos**, who teaches Probability and Statistics at the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Democritus University of Thrace, Greece.

AI assistance is used to draft the posts, code and interactive elements. Every post is reviewed and approved by the author before publication.

## Follow new posts

New posts appear every Monday, Wednesday and Friday. To follow them, add the [RSS feed](index.xml) (`https://www.stochastika.com/en/index.xml`) to a feed reader such as Feedly or Inoreader, or click the <i class="bi bi-rss"></i> icon at the top right. New posts are also shared on our [Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/stochastika/).
